title: Length-Prioritized Batch Scheduler Refactor for Mixed Prompt/Response Latency SLOs
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Problem: Our current continuous batching scheduler treats all incoming requests with a single length-agnostic priority leading to poor tail latency for short-response interactive requests and inflated GPU memory usage when long sequences are packed naively. This is especially visible in mixed workloads where prompt lengths vary widely and response generations differ (chat vs. single-turn).

Goal: Refactor the batch scheduler to be length-prioritized and SLO-aware, integrate tighter KV cache residency policies, and add GPU memory accounting hooks so the runtime can make packing and slot decisions that balance throughput, latency, and memory fragmentation. Deliver a design and implementation that reduces 99th percentile latency for short-response queries by >=30% under mixed loads while keeping token throughput within 10% of current baseline and lowering peak GPU memory variance by >=15%.

Scope: Scheduler refactor (core algorithm + metrics), KV cache lifecycle changes (segmented residency + evictions tied to scheduler decisions), GPU memory accounting API and runtime guards, end-to-end experiments, rollout plan with canary and fallback. Not in scope: model architecture changes, allocator-level CUDA kernel work beyond instrumentation.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler accepts length-labels (prompt_len, expected_response_len) and computes a priority score used for slot allocation
End-to-end benchmarks show >=30% reduction in p99 latency for short-response queries in mixed workloads (measured across at least three representative production traces)
Token throughput (tokens/s) remains within 10% of baseline for target mixes
GPU peak memory variance reduced by >=15% across runs by improved packing decisions and eviction policies
KV cache eviction API exposes per-slot residency hints and integrates with scheduler so hot prefixes are preserved for high-priority slots
Feature gated behind runtime flag with safe fallback to current scheduler and documented metrics for rollout
